name: Shale Shaker Cutting Estimations (Desktop)
overview: Desktop-based (v1) computer vision system to monitor and analyze rock cuttings from shale shakers in real-time using CCTV footage, integrated with the WITSML realtime drilling data standard. Built with classical OpenCV image processing, without deep learning. The system was designed to improve the efficiency and accuracy of drilling process monitoring by providing real-time data on rock coverage and composition, thereby supporting operational decision-making in the oil and gas industry.
challenge: The primary challenges included processing video streams in real-time with minimal latency, accurately detecting and analyzing rock cuttings amidst varying lighting conditions and potential noise, and keeping the system reliable and scalable enough to plug into monitoring systems like the Early Monitoring System (EMS).
result: The deployed system provided real-time monitoring of shale shaker cuttings, enabling more informed decision-making during drilling operations. It achieved high accuracy in detecting rock coverage and composition, with visualizations helping to identify trends in rock composition over time. The system was integrated with the Early Monitoring System, enhancing overall operational efficiency and reducing manual monitoring efforts.

name: Aerial Image Segmentation
overview: Research prototype for my university UAV team: deep-learning segmentation of aerial imagery, satellite and drone, into buildings, roads, and vegetation for geospatial mapping. Built with PyTorch on 500+ annotated images.
challenge: Key challenges included handling variations in image resolution and lighting conditions, developing accurate segmentation models with limited annotated datasets, and optimizing model performance on resource-constrained hardware.
result: The research produced a prototype segmentation model based on deep learning, demonstrating promising accuracy on a limited test dataset. It provided valuable insights into the challenges of aerial image segmentation and recommendations for future development, such as data augmentation and model fine-tuning.

name: Tomato Leaf Disease Detection
overview: Developed a lightweight deep learning model using TensorFlow Lite to detect diseases in tomato leaves from images. The model, based on transfer learning with MobileNetV2, achieves high accuracy with a compact size, suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices.
challenge: Optimizing a high-accuracy model to maintain performance within a compact 5MB size, handling a large dataset with 11 classes, and keeping detection steady across varied image conditions such as lighting and angles.
result: The model achieved 99.4% accuracy in detecting 11 classes of tomato leaf diseases using a dataset of over 17,000 images. Deployed on Streamlit, the application allows users to upload images and receive real-time disease predictions, demonstrating potential for agricultural diagnostic tools.

name: Smart Document Scanner & OCR Service
overview: Production-ready scanning pipeline: detects a card or document in a photograph, corrects its perspective, enhances legibility, reads it with a neural OCR engine (RapidOCR / PP-OCRv6 on ONNX Runtime), and emits structured JSON where every field carries a confidence and the rule that produced it. The same Dockerfile runs locally, in Compose, and on Railway.
challenge: Hard captures (cluttered desks, low light, blur, rotation, low contrast) pull in background text and drop characters, so the pipeline scores crops by recovered text coverage instead of confidence, keeps a full-frame fallback, and reports failures such as NO_DOCUMENT or NO_CONTENT rather than empty successes.
result: Deployed from a three-stage Docker build with a C++17 accelerator, a batch CLI, and an anti-hardcoding CI gate. On the benchmark it scores 72.3% mean per-key with 67.2% exact matches and detection recall of 11 of 11 images, with every result traceable back to the pixels that produced it.

name: PasFotoIn Browser Photo Editor
overview: Browser-based editor for Indonesian ID photos and social crops. Every process runs on the user's device: no uploads, no server, no account. Presets in centimeters (2x3, 3x4, 4x6, 6x9), ICAO-compliant international sizes, automatic subject cutout via an in-browser segmentation model, and an A4 print sheet ready to cut.

result: Live at www.pasfotoin.web.id with 26 presets across ratios, Indonesian document sizes, ICAO sizes, and social media; an 8-stage matte post-processing pipeline; batch ZIP export; and a 300 DPI A4 print sheet, all on-device and covered by Vitest and Playwright suites.

name: Intelligent Document Assistant (RAG)
overview: RAG-based document Q&A assistant: upload PDF, TXT, or Markdown, then ask questions in Indonesian and get answers with clickable citations. The system refuses to answer when the context is not enough, and general-knowledge answers are clearly labelled so they are never confused with document-sourced ones. Includes per-document private conversations, retrieval quality evaluation, and observability.
challenge: Keeping the assistant trustworthy: no citation without context, a measured similarity threshold (0.82) instead of a default one because irrelevant text still scores 0.72-0.81, document scope stored in the session so private chats stay private, and a multilingual embedding model because English-only models perform far worse for Indonesian.
result: Delivered a full-stack RAG system with FastAPI, ChromaDB, and SQLite behind a Next.js 16 frontend: 534 backend tests at 83% coverage, 59 Playwright scenarios, 21 end-to-end checks, and a RAGAS evaluation dataset where questions that must be refused are scored as strictly as the ones that must be answered.

name: DataLoom Data Operator Workspace
overview: Data operator workspace to build, run, and monitor end to end pipelines. Raw data lands in Bronze, is cleaned deterministically into Silver, passes a four rule quality gate, and is promoted to Gold only when fit for use. Every rejected row lands in Quarantine with a reason code, agents only propose while humans approve, and validation rules plus project thresholds are readable in the data contract page.
challenge: Guaranteeing that bad data never reaches reports: rejected rows need recorded reasons instead of silent drops, promotion needs deterministic reconciliation instead of model opinion, and rule changes need versioning plus human approval instead of silent formula edits.
result: Shipped a live platform at dataloom.web.id with a demo mode that runs fully in the browser: guided setup, DAG canvas, run monitor with gate checklist, quarantine with reason codes, data contract, agent approval workspace, read only text to SQL, and usage billing. Verified per README: web typecheck and lint pass with 25 of 25 pages built, 320 backend unit tests pass, and a 58 step browser suite passes with zero console errors.

name: RigDaily Daily Drilling Report System
overview: Daily well operations reporting that connects rig and office in one controlled report flow: DDR, 24 hour time breakdown, NPT, cost and AFE, billing, personnel, marine, safety, and rig to office sync. Runs as a Next.js web app for the office and an offline-first Electron desktop .exe with local SQLite for the rig, syncing through an outbox when the network returns. Seven roles from Rig Clerk to Administrator have server-checked permissions, and every approved report locks with a numbered amendment trail.
challenge: Keeping one report consistent across two disconnected environments: the 1,440 minute day must validate with no gaps and no overlaps before submission, depth must never move backward, and rig submissions must never overwrite an office-approved final but land in a manual conflict queue. Seven roles share one dataset, so every permission is checked on the server rather than hidden in the menu.
result: Delivered a live platform at rigdaily.web.id with a public landing plus demo mode covering 7 roles, a five-stage report flow from Draft to Locked with audit log and PDF distribution, and a desktop NSIS x64 .exe that writes to on-device SQLite first and syncs via outbox. Covered by 360 Vitest unit tests plus Playwright end-to-end suites.
